Fintech Meetup Europe 2026: My Key Takeaways

A recap of Fintech Meetup Europe 2026 (6–8 October, Lisbon) — what the industry is talking about, who I met, and BD exploration I did for QuickBooks internationally.

What the conference covered

The themes shaping European fintech right now

Fintech Meetup Europe ran four parallel tracks — Banks & Challengers, Enterprise & Infrastructure, Commerce & Fintech, and Startups & Investors — built around twelve recurring themes across the programme.

AI

From agent-led banking products to whether AI widens or closes the gap for new entrants.

Regulation

MiCA, FiDA and the EU AI Act as either a strategic asset or a barrier to speed.

Sovereignty

Stablecoins, sovereign payment rails and Europe's push for strategic autonomy.

European Scale

44 countries, 50+ payment rails — what it takes to operate as one market.

Build vs Buy

Banks are building more in-house — what that leaves on the table for fintech.

Consolidation

Where mid-sized European banks fit as the market consolidates.

Customer Relationship

Who owns checkout and the customer as A2A and embedded finance scale.

Liquidity

The evolving European lending landscape and where VC funding is still flowing.

Fraud

Real-time, machine-speed fraud and what detection looks like next.

Innovation

What still counts as real product differentiation once every fintech looks the same.

Operational Resilience

ISO 20022 migration and building for compliance-by-design.

Market Structure

Legacy banks re-platforming to compete at fintech speed.

The highlight

Moderating Monzo × Wise Platform

The session I moderated on Day 2 — a conversation between two of the companies defining how money moves across borders.

Main Stage · Wed 7 Oct · 09:40–10:00

Building Global Payments at the Speed of Change

Moderated by Nikita Pillai, Principal, International Fintech Partnerships, Intuit

A discussion on what it takes to build payment infrastructure that keeps adapting — not just scaling — as new schemes, regulation and customer expectations keep arriving faster than any roadmap can plan for. Covered where differentiation goes once instant payments become the baseline, and where Europe can lead globally on payments infrastructure.

Pranay Ahluwalia — GM Payments, Monzo
Manuel Sandhofer — GM Europe, Middle East & LatAm, Wise Platform
Who we met

Meetings & partnership synergies

Fourteen 1:1 meetings and events across the two days, with key takeaways and next steps from each.

AB

Conrad Ford

CPO & CSO, Allica Bank
Tue 6 Oct · 10:45–11:00

UK SME challenger bank — ~£4bn in SME loans and £5bn deposits, recently acquired Kriya for embedded working capital and invoice finance.

Key Takeaways
  • Keen to explore mid-market distribution and accounting-distribution partnerships for Allica × QuickBooks in the UK.
  • Most excited about building an embedded/integrated cash management platform between a mid-market bank like Allica and an accounting platform — he sees a gap between what banking platforms and accounting platforms each serve, around agentic or supported cash management for mid-market and SMBs alike.
  • The mid-market is where the highest-value customers and the largest deposits sit, so that's where a cash management solution would create the most value for both Allica and Intuit.
  • The integrated flow he has in mind would require a mid-market customer to hold both an Allica bank account and a QuickBooks licence.
  • This was explored exactly a year ago where Conrad Ford presented this deck to Patrick Johnson and Neil Oates. However with priorities shifting and internal restructuring at Intuit, this was not explored further. Patrick however did find the idea very interesting and was keen to look deeper into it.

Next step: set up time between Ishan, Conrad, and the new payments PMM/PM once they're in seat (a few weeks out). Not an FY27 opportunity, but a strong candidate for FY28 given our P0 to grow mid-market — Allica's accountant base (firms serving larger clients) fits well, though it's a heavier product/engineering lift.

SG

Alexandre Fernandes

VP Western Europe, Solidgate
Tue 6 Oct · 11:00–11:15

Payment orchestration and acquiring platform for fast-scaling online businesses — 500+ merchants across 150+ countries.

Key Takeaways

A general education meeting on the payments orchestration / cross-border acquiring platform Solidgate runs. No specific follow-up planned.

PL

Erik Olson

Plaid (title unverified)
Tue 6 Oct · time TBD

US financial data network — 12,000+ institutions connected, 95% US bank coverage, new financial-foundation models launched in 2026.

Key Takeaways

A recap meeting on where things stand exploring Plaid as a bank-connectivity partner. Neil Oates already owns this conversation with Plaid directly.

Neil needs more regional coverage in APAC, the Middle East and Africa than Plaid or Yapli currently offer, so he'll likely look to additional regional players beyond Yapli there.

Full status of bank connectivity, Neil's conversations, and the partner landscape: bank connectivity doc and intl market connectivity micropage (internal, Intuit access only).

FB

Prashant Fuloria

CEO, Fundbox
Tue 6 Oct · 12:00–12:30

Embedded working-capital platform, rebranded in 2025 as "embedded capital infrastructure" — 190,000+ small businesses helped.

Key Takeaways
  • Fundbox is launching its first UK product (embedded lending) in Q1 2027, on top of an existing UK partner — believed to be EverCommerce.
  • Very keen to explore embedded working capital with Intuit for the UK on the back of that launch, and interested in expanding with us in the US and Canada too (Canada solution also live only from early next year).
  • Beyond embedded lending, they can also refer customers to a Fundbox-branded page/platform — Fundbox owns risk, decisioning, disbursement and servicing — though embedded infrastructure is their more common model.
  • Prashant is keen to treat this as a lighthouse partner for their international expansion, but wants clarity on how firm embedded lending actually is on our roadmap.

Next step: Dani is the main point of contact, in touch with Fundbox on the UK opportunity (targeting sole traders). Prashant can get involved if useful.

AG

Diego Fernandes

Ant Group (identity unverified)
Tue 6 Oct · 3:00–3:30

Ant International's global payments infra — Alipay+, Antom and WorldFirst — connected to 150M+ merchants across 220+ markets.

Key Takeaways

An exploratory BD conversation to understand Alipay's global payments infrastructure. They acquired WorldFirst a couple of years ago and have significant global coverage, with their sweet spot in Southeast Asia, Asia Pacific and China — worth a closer look as and when we look into those markets. Their FX rails could support multi-currency invoicing directly in QuickBooks, and they can facilitate cross-border payments across a number of markets.

FC

Andreas Ioannou

Senior Associate, Fintech Collective
Tue 6 Oct · 4:30–5:00

NY/London seed-to-Series B fintech VC; portfolio includes Simetrik (reconciliation) and Contabilizei (Brazilian SMB accounting).

Key Takeaways

Very useful for market mapping — a deliberate scan of AR/AP, billing, tax, treasury, accounting-automation, reconciliation, ERP and FP&A platforms that have emerged across the UK and Europe over the last year or two. Good signal on what's coming and growing in the market.

Most interesting single name: manano.ai — a WhatsApp-first workflow and payments platform for tradespeople.

  • Product: tradespeople create quotes and invoices, capture expenses by photo or voice note, and get automatic VAT reports plus QuickBooks/Xero exports, all inside WhatsApp. Escrow on quotes and instant pay (factoring-style) are on the roadmap.
  • Team: David Coallier (CEO, serial founder with exits to Engine Yard and Sophos, previously ran Clearword), Claudia (CFO, accounting background with trades clients), and Ross (CTO). Based in Ireland, expanding into the UK first.
  • Traction: 9% free-to-paid conversion with no marketing, landing at about €24/month, a ~1.75% take rate on payments, and a distribution deal covering 26 stores.

He also passed on a broader dump of names worth scanning for market mapping, grouped by category:

  • Spend management & AP: Adfin, Adaptive.build, Sayanchor, Getapron, Bill, Candis, Brex, Finway, Jeeves, Libeo, Melio, Moss, Payhawk, Pleo, Pliant, Ramp, Regate, Routable, Settle, Soldo, Spendesk, Vic AI, Yokoy.
  • Billing & AR: Amberflo, JustPaid, Kredos AI, LedgerUp, Stuut, Togai, Sequence, Billtrust, Chargebee, Lago, M3ter, Maxio, Hyperline, Metronome, Paddle, Recurly, Solvimon, Zuora, Tabs, Upflow, Monite, Tesorio, Turnstile, Tola, Lunos, Monto.
  • Tax management: Numeral, Accordance, Taxwire, April, Kintsugi, Black Ore, Anrok, Fonoa, Avalara, Loctax, Sovos, Taxdoo, TaxGPT, Hedgi, Taxy.
  • Treasury & cash management: Nilus, Finmo, Embat, Round, Panax, Agicap, Atlar, Formance, Kyriba, Meow, Modern Treasury, Payable, Payflows, Sibill, TreasurySpring, Trovata, Vesto, Vitesse, Crispa, Tidely, Trezy.
  • Accounting automation: Briefcase AI, Bluebook AI, Artifact AI, Zamp, Truewind AI, Zeni AI, Basis AI, Mika AI, Jenesys AI, Ravical (which saw an uptick in app connections a couple of months ago), Saveria, Phoros.de (AI rollup).
  • Reconciliation & close: Numeric AI, Ledge AI, Maxima AI, Stacks AI, Nominal AI, Simetrik, Maximor.
  • ERP & general ledger: Rillet, Light, Campfire, Doss, DualEntry, Tailor, Puzzle, Digits, Keel.
  • FP&A: Runway AI (now operating as cfo.ai), Pigment, Datarails, Abacum AI, Mosaic, Aleph.

Shapers & Opera Tech Ventures

Philippe & Thomas Teixeira da Mota

WS

Manuel Sandhofer

GM Europe, Middle East & LatAm, Wise Platform
Wed 7 Oct · 10:00–10:20 + lunch 12:00–1:00

Wise Platform powers cross-border infrastructure for Monzo, N26, Nubank and (new in FY26) UniCredit — £181bn+ in FX volume moved.

Key Takeaways
  • Explored using the cross-border Wise platform to pay invoices in multiple currencies internationally — priority market is Canada, where we see more multi-currency-enabled accounts and where Wise sees its highest cross-border payments penetration of any market today.
  • Wise is also interested in a distribution partnership: either a simple referral/marketing arrangement, or a marketing partnership with a product element involving "Pay with Wise," if Solutions Engineering could build it.

Next step: managing expectations that this is further out in planning and roadmap — wait for the Canada lead and payments PM/PMM to be in seat before taking this further.

FN

Olga Shikhantsova

Head of Product Strategy, Finom
Wed 7 Oct · from 4:00

EMI-licensed SME banking — business accounts, invoicing, expense management and AI-enabled bookkeeping; 125,000 customers across 5 EU markets.

Key Takeaways

Very interesting one. Finom is an EMI-licensed SMB/SME bank, led by a team with deep fintech and VC experience in Europe. Currently focused on mainland Europe, with Germany, Spain and France as their largest markets. They have very good product-market fit as an accounting-tech (bookkeeping) platform across mainland Europe — Germany, Spain, France, Italy and the Netherlands.
